Crash.type: Compiler crash (internal error in IPA mod-ref analysis, ealias pass)
Crash.explanation: Three nested functions inside one function, the first carrying a section attribute and called by the third, trip a gcc_checking_assert in gimple_call_static_chain_flags (gimple.cc:1683, 'nested functions should always bind to current def') during the ealias pass at -O1 and above; -O0 and -Og compile cleanly. The compiler survives nested-function lowering and fails later in IPA mod-ref analysis — a different failure site than a tree-nested.cc lowering crash. Program is GNU C (nested functions); clang rejects the extension by design.

reproduce.expected: The file compiles successfully (as it does at -O0).
reproduce.observed:
internal compiler error: in gimple_call_static_chain_flags, at gimple.cc:1683
Reproduces at -O1/-O2/-O3/-Os (not -O0/-Og).

Crash.type: Compiler crash (internal error in the C front end)
Crash.explanation: A conditional expression whose second operand applies logical negation to a _Float16 expression (!(m + 1)) while the third operand mixes _Float16 arithmetic trips the operand-1 gcc_assert in build_conditional_expr, at c/c-typeck.cc:5714. This is the sibling assertion of the operand-2 failure at line 5720 (same excess-precision block, opposite operand position). The program is valid C23: clang-19.1.7 accepts it cleanly.

reproduce.observed:
internal compiler error: in build_conditional_expr, at c/c-typeck.cc:5714
Reproduces at every optimization level (-O0/-O1/-O2/-O3).

Crash.type: Compiler crash (internal error in C++ name mangling)
Crash.explanation: A requires-clause on a member function of a nested local struct inside a template, referencing sizeof of a function-local static constexpr array, crashes GCC 14.3.0 in the name mangler: discriminator_for_local_entity (cp/mangle.cc:2264) hits gcc_checking_assert(DECL_ARTIFICIAL(entity)) on an entity with no lang-specific data. The program is valid C++20 — clang++-19 accepts it cleanly. A known sibling report at the same function (line 2316) is RESOLVED; this line-2264 assertion survives that fix.

reproduce.observed:
internal compiler error: in discriminator_for_local_entity, at cp/mangle.cc:2264
Reproduces at every optimization level (-O0/-O1/-O2/-O3) with -std=c++20 or later.

Crash.type: Compiler bug (assembler output references an undefined compiler-generated label; link fails)
Crash.explanation: A two-label asm goto (je to one label, jmp to the other) with '+m' outputs makes GCC emit a jump to a label that never reaches the generated assembly, so linking fails with 'undefined reference to .L3' at every optimization level, including -O0. Clang compiles and runs the same source correctly. Also reproduces on GCC 13.1 — a longstanding asm-goto label-emission issue, distinct from any runtime miscompilation.

reproduce.expected: The file compiles and links successfully (as it does with clang).
reproduce.observed:
/usr/bin/ld: ... in function 'test(int)': test4.cpp:(.text+0x32): undefined reference to '.L3'
collect2: error: ld returned 1 exit status
Reproduces at every optimization level (-O0/-O1/-O2/-O3).

Miscompilation.type: Miscompilation (asm goto with memory output operands; silent wrong value)
Miscompilation.explanation: asm goto with '+m' output operands and a thread_local memory input is miscompiled by GCC 14.3.0 on the label path: test(1) must return saved-1 = -1, but the generated code returns 0 at -O0/-O1 and 1 at -O2/-O3. No crash — a silent wrong value whose value itself depends on the optimization level, while clang 19.1.0 compiles the same source correctly at every level and the source is UBSan-clean (clang-19.1.7 -fsanitize=undefined -O0). Also reproduces on GCC 13.1: a longstanding asm-goto output-operand issue.

reproduce.expected: The program prints "normal=1" then "abort=-1" (as clang 19.1.0 does at every optimization level).
reproduce.observed: -O0 and -O1 builds print "abort=0"; -O2 and -O3 builds print "abort=1"; none prints the correct -1.

Crash.type: Compiler crash (Clang CodeGen, DenseMap corruption in getVLASize)
Crash.explanation: A function-local static declared inside a lambda nested in a template function, bound to a reference non-type template parameter, crashes Clang 19.1.0 in code generation: CodeGenFunction::getVLASize (CodeGenFunction.cpp:2322) grows the VLASizeMap (DenseMap<const Expr*, Value*>) with a dangling Expr key left over from template substitution. The program is valid C++ — g++-13 accepts it cleanly. Crashes at every optimization level and every language mode; also crashes clang 19.1.7.

reproduce.observed: The compiler crashes with a stack dump whose top frames are DenseMap<clang::Expr const*, llvm::Value*>::moveFromOldBuckets <- grow <- InsertIntoBucket <- CodeGenFunction::getVLASize (caught by the crash recovery handler).

Crash.type: Compiler crash (Clang CodeGen, static member instantiation)
Crash.explanation: Instantiating the out-of-line definition of a static data member of a class template, when the member's type is a dependent nested alias written without typename, crashes Clang 19.1.0 in CodeGenModule::HandleCXXStaticMemberVarInstantiation (CodeGenModule.cpp:5956). g++ rejects the program (missing typename), so at minimum Clang should diagnose instead of crashing — a distinct crash site from the return-type getTypeInfoImpl failure.

reproduce.expected: A diagnostic error (missing typename), as g++ produces.
reproduce.observed: The compiler crashes with a stack dump in CodeGenModule::HandleCXXStaticMemberVarInstantiation. Reproduces at every optimization level and language mode; also on clang 19.1.7.

Crash.type: Compiler crash (Clang CodeGen, ConvertTypeForMem on static array member)
Crash.explanation: Same ill-typed static member pattern as llvm-crash-2, but with an ARRAY member: taking the address of the static array member 'm[2]' crashes Clang 19.1.0 in CodeGenTypes::ConvertTypeForMem (CodeGenTypes.cpp:107), reached from GetAddrOfGlobalVar <- HandleCXXStaticMemberVarInstantiation — a different crash function in the same cluster. g++ rejects the program (missing typename).

reproduce.expected: A diagnostic error (missing typename), as g++ produces.
reproduce.observed: The compiler crashes with a stack dump in CodeGenTypes::ConvertTypeForMem. Reproduces at every optimization level; also on clang 19.1.7.

Crash.type: Compiler crash (Clang CodeGen, EmitGlobalVarDeclLValue on use)
Crash.explanation: Same ill-typed static member pattern, but the member is *used* (not explicitly instantiated) through a function template: '(void)W<U>::m' inside 'template<class U> void use()' crashes Clang 19.1.0 in EmitGlobalVarDeclLValue (CGExpr.cpp:2857) via EmitDeclRefLValue — expression emission rather than instantiation handling, a third distinct crash site in the cluster. g++ rejects the program (missing typename).

reproduce.expected: A diagnostic error (missing typename), as g++ produces.
reproduce.observed: The compiler crashes with a stack dump in EmitGlobalVarDeclLValue (CGExpr.cpp:2857). Reproduces at every optimization level; also on clang 19.1.7.

Miscompilation.type: Miscompilation (generated program crashes at runtime, -Os only)
Miscompilation.explanation: Clang 19.1.0 mis-compiles this switch/loop program so the binary segfaults ONLY at -Os; -O0/-O1/-O2/-O3/-Oz all produce correct binaries, and gcc builds are correct at every level including -Os. The source is UBSan-clean (clang-19.1.7 -fsanitize=undefined -O0). A sibling pattern (same switch/fallthrough chain) segfaults only at -O1 — the affected optimization level itself differs here.

reproduce.expected: Correct behavior: the program simply returns (exit 0), as the -O0/-O1/-O2/-O3/-Oz builds do.
reproduce.observed: Only the -Os build is affected: the resulting binary dies with SIGSEGV right at start (exit 139).

Miscompilation.type: Miscompilation (x86-64 backend: shift+mask equality compiled as a non-equivalent rotate, _BitInt(13))
Miscompilation.explanation: Clang 19.1.0 for x86-64 compiles (v << 2) == (v & -4) on a 13-bit integer as a rotate comparison, giving wrong answers for inputs a=2730 and a=5461 at -O1/-O2 (-O0 is correct; UBSan-clean). The wrong fold fires whenever the shift amount does not divide the bit width; this width-13 instance is one representative. An i13 IR-level reproducer is included; the same wrong fold is visible when test11.ll is compiled with llc for x86-64. Also reproduces on clang 19.1.7.

reproduce.environment: Clang 19.1.0 (x86-64-unknown-linux-gnu); llc 19.1.0 for the IR-level reproducer
reproduce.command: clang -O1 test11.c -o a.out && ./a.out   # also -O2; IR level: llc -mtriple=x86_64-linux-gnu -filetype=obj test11.ll && link test11_driver.c
reproduce.expected: Every input a in 0..8191 must match the reference computed in 64-bit arithmetic (the -O0 build prints "RESULT: correct").
reproduce.observed: -O1/-O2 builds print "a=2730 got=3 exp=1" and "a=5461 got=3 exp=1", then "RESULT: wrong 2". The generated code compares X against rotl(X, 2) instead of evaluating (X << 2) == (X & -4) on the 13-bit value. The llc-compiled IR reproducer mismatches on exactly the same two inputs.

Miscompilation.type: Miscompilation (SLP vectorizer narrows a comparison; silent wrong value)
Miscompilation.explanation: Stride variant of the SLP-narrowing miscompile: with loop strides i += 3, j += 1 over the 6x6 array, Clang 19.1.0 -O2/-O3 SLP-vectorizes the unsigned-short comparison as a signed 16-bit compare and prints acc=0 instead of acc=12; -O0/-O1/-Os are correct, GCC 13.1 -O2 is correct, and the source is UBSan-clean.

reproduce.expected: The program prints "acc=12 (expected 12)" (as the -O0 and -O1 builds do).
reproduce.observed: The -O2/-O3 builds print "acc=0 (expected 12)". No crash — the value is silently wrong.
